events.title: Columbus Sets Sail from Spain
events.description: Christopher Columbus departed from the port of Palos de la Frontera with three ships, the Santa María, the Pinta and the Niña. He was searching for a western sea route to Asia.
events.significance: The voyage led to the first lasting contact between Europe and the Americas, and it reshaped world history, trade and populations.

events.title: Germany Declares War on France
events.description: As the July Crisis spiralled, Germany declared war on France. This widened the conflict that had begun days earlier in Eastern Europe, and German forces moved toward Belgium.
events.significance: The declaration helped turn a regional dispute into World War I, a conflict that cost millions of lives and redrew the map of Europe.

events.title: Roger Casement Executed
events.description: Roger Casement was executed in London for treason over his part in planning the Irish Easter Rising. He was a former British diplomat who had become an Irish nationalist.
events.significance: Casement had earlier exposed colonial abuses in the Congo and Peru. His execution made him a lasting symbol of Irish republicanism.

events.title: Niger Gains Independence from France
events.description: The West African nation of Niger became fully independent from France. It was one of many African territories to win sovereignty around that time.
events.significance: Niger's independence was part of the decolonization wave of 1960, which reshaped the political map of Africa.
